newsitem.title: BELGIUM: SOCCER-KLUIVERT THREATENS TO QUIT AS INTERNATIONAL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-KLUIVERT THREATENS TO QUIT AS INTERNATIONAL.

text.p: AC Milan's new striker Patrick Kluivert was quoted on Tuesday as saying he would quit as Dutch international if he was hissed at in their World Cup qualifier against Belgium on September 6.
"I will not play for the Netherlands any more if I'm being whistled at," Kluivert told Het Laatste Nieuws newspaper.

Kluivert, who moved to Milan from Ajax, has been under intense media pressure and criticised at home after a conviction last year of causing death by dangerous driving, followed this year by rape charges that were later dropped.
"It leaves a bad taste. They're after me...I've made mistakes allright, but a lot of the things that are being said are not true," Kluivert said.
He dismissed suggestions he might not be worthy of a place in the Dutch side.
"If I play well at Milan, I have to be called up. They're applying just one standard I hope? Otherwise the question will be whether I should still come to the Dutch team," he said.
Arch-rivals the Netherlands and Belgium are both on 15 points from six matches in European qualifying group seven.
The Dutch, who beat Belgium 3-0 at home last December, are still ahead on goal difference but Belgium have since improved their game after switching coaches and revamping the team.

"We taught the Belgians a lesson in Brussels, but I'm not in the least surprised that they are back in the running for the World Cup," Kluivert said. "Individually they have too much quality to be written off just like that."
